# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only that the large button is smooth; the wire contents are not tactilely apparent. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s instructions and the Deaf to identify all visible markings and colours, ideally through whatever protocol they are using.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="What does the manual require? Please relay the Deaf's visual findings and tell me the exact action.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0. Light green. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute sent gestures: one-up then crossed-fingers; two victory signs; two horns. I saw you make the pointing gesture.

The bomb’s visible state is now known: display 0, green light, a large button labelled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and wires coloured green, yellow, and red in positions 1–3. I still do not know the manual’s rule, and the gestures from Mute are not readable to me, so I will ask Mute to state the instruction plainly. I will not touch anything yet.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received the Deaf's bomb findings. Please state the manual's exact required action in words, including whether to push the button or cut a wire and which position.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New gesture from Mute: victory sign, victory sign, then index-up.

I need the Mute to communicate the manual in plain words; the prior gesture request was invalid because it used a symbol outside the allowed alphabet. I will send only a legal pointing gesture to the Deaf, while asking the Mute directly for the exact instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's exact action in plain words now. Do not encode it with gestures.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gestures were victory sign, then index-up. I also received your pointing gesture.

The Deaf’s reports show that Mute is communicating only through gestures, but no gesture-to-instruction code has yet been established. I will define a simple unambiguous code: thumbs-up means push; thumbs-down followed by one, two, or three fingers means cut that wire. Mute should send the manual’s required action in that code, and Deaf can report the symbols in words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual's required action: 👍 means push the button. 👎 followed by ☝ means cut wire 1, followed by ✌ means cut wire 2, followed by 🤟 means cut wire 3. Send exactly the required action.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gestures: victory sign, victory sign, then index-up. The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Mute’s repeated sequence does not match the encoding I proposed, because that encoding was given as unwritable gesture marks in speech rather than as an actual visual signal. I will now provide a clear four-symbol key directly: one symbol alone will identify the required action. I will wait for that answer before touching the bomb.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer with exactly one gesture: thumbs-up means PUSH; thumbs-down means CUT wire 1; OK means CUT wire 2; index-up means CUT wire 3. Send only that one gesture.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gestures: thumbs-down, then index-up. Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Mute has now sent the exact two-gesture sequence I defined for “cut wire 1”: thumbs-down followed by index-up. The Deaf confirms the bomb still shows display 0, green light, and wires colored green, yellow, red; however, the manual’s communicated choice is the explicit action code, not an inference from the wire color. I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
